additionalActions.title: Expose the detection webhook to browsers
additionalActions.text: Marketplace starts the webhook sidecar (default port 3080). The plugin UI needs a URL the browser can reach.
instructions: Marketplace starts the server/ webhook sidecar in Docker. You do not need to run npm start yourself.
In the plugin UI, set the backend URL to an address the browser can open (not only localhost on the CloudTAK host).
If users open CloudTAK remotely, reverse-proxy a path to the sidecar and use that HTTPS URL in the plugin.
Paste the snippet below into the Caddy site block that already reverse-proxies cloudtak-api, then reload Caddy.

additionalActions.title: Route /print-api through Caddy
additionalActions.text: The print Docker service is started by Marketplace. Browsers still need Caddy (or equivalent) to reach /print-api.
instructions: Marketplace starts the print Docker service. Do not paste the compose block by hand.
Paste the snippet below at the TOP LEVEL of your Caddyfile, outside every site block.
Inside the site block that already has reverse_proxy cloudtak-api:5000, add: import cloudtak_print
Reload Caddy: docker compose exec caddy caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
Check both https://YOURHOST/print-api/health and https://YOURHOST/print-api. The second must return application/json, not HTML.

additionalActions.title: Optional: transparent print margins
additionalActions.text: Add GDAL_PDF_BANDS=4 to the CloudTAK events service environment so printed sheet margins stay transparent when imported back onto the map.
instructions: In the CloudTAK events service environment, add: GDAL_PDF_BANDS=4
Recreate the events container after saving compose.

additionalActions.title: Allow the Blitzortung websocket in nginx CSP
additionalActions.text: Production CloudTAK nginx sets Content-Security-Policy connect-src to 'self', which blocks the live lightning feed. Marketplace does not patch nginx.
instructions: Edit CloudTAK api/nginx.conf.js and add the snippet below to the connect-src list in Content-Security-Policy.
Rebuild or restart the CloudTAK api container after saving.
Until that change is in place, Start in the plugin can no-op in production even though install succeeded.
